derived_stem.hen54_9: Hen. 54,9 is listed under b) perdi, in the III,1 reflexive/passive entry. That reference proves how Dillmann classified the occurrence in his source treatment; it does not make Charles 1906's different selected vocalization III,1.

quantifier.support: Original Latin entry explicitly marks Acc. and supplies the -o form. It also explains use for multiple individuals and continuation includes substantival/adjectival uses.
quantifier.case_result: Selected ኵሎ is an object quantifier, not the nominative subject all.

primary_lexicon.edition_difference_limit: Dillmann 1865 does not here print a full Ethiopic quotation of Hen54:9 in the III,1 line. Its citation alone cannot prove his exact edition token. Charles 1906 actually prints a reported passive/reflexive alternative and selects the distinct active token; primary grammar verifies the difference. Do not assert a particular 1865 edition reading has been re-collated without its actual text page.

primary_grammar.work: Dillmann, Ethiopic Grammar, second edition edited by Bezold, translated by Crichton, 1907

section99.page198: Ground-stem quadriliteral perfect includes ደምሰሰ with extinguish sense; subjunctive changes the vowel after the penultimate radical; imperfect additionally inserts a after second radical.

section100.rule: Reflexive stem does not change the penultimate radical vowel between subjunctive and imperfect, but the imperfect inserts a after the second radical. Root example is explicitly supplied with passive extinguished semantics.

section101.page203: Imperfect/indicative and subjunctive personal signs include third-person prefix.
section101.page204: Third-person plural uses prefixed y sign with masculine -u and feminine -a.
section101.result: Selected yi...u is third masculine plural, not a second person or a singular verb.

primary_grammar.important_correction: At low displayed size the two paradigms looked alike; an interim parent message raised possible written identity.
